review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read the definitions of spatialPartial, timePartial and spatialSecondPartial, and the scaling definitions and measurability and continuity lemmas in ScalingInvarianceBasic.lean. I could not compile anything, so every proposed rewrite is a sketch and untested. The first three findings are the substantial repetition. The measurability block is smaller. The time pullback also repeats the chain-rule skeleton, but with different slice maps. Merging it with the spatial case would need a more abstract lemma, and I did not claim that.

rw [fderiv_comp]

    have hpoint : μ⁻¹ • (scalingSpace μ z₀.1 z.1 - z₀.1) = z.1 := by
findings.problem: The same spatial chain-rule computation appears three times. testSpatialDerivative (lines 53-69) proves it for an arbitrary smooth φ: rewrite with `fderiv_comp`, use `testSpatialInverse_deriv`, show `hpoint`, then `simp only [comp_apply, smul_apply, id_apply]` and `map_smul`. spatialPartial_pullback (lines 103-116) repeats this block verbatim for the slice `fun y => ψ (y, z.2)` and ignores testSpatialDerivative. spatialSecondPartial_pullback does use testSpatialDerivative, but then needs the `rw [testSpatialInverse_eq]` and `simpa [Function.comp_def]` step (hderiv'/hderiv, lines 206-213) to turn the homeomorphism form back into the lambda form. So the derivative-of-a-spatially-pulled-back-slice fact is proved in two incompatible forms.
findings.proposed_change: Restate testSpatialDerivative in lambda form, without the homeomorphism, and drop testSpatialHomeomorph if nothing else uses it. For example: `private theorem fderiv_spatialPullback_apply (μ) (hμ : 0 < μ) (x₀) {φ : Vec3 → ℝ} (hφ : ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) φ) (j) (x) : fderiv ℝ (fun y => φ (μ⁻¹ • (y - x₀))) (scalingSpace μ x₀ x) (basisVec j) = μ⁻¹ * fderiv ℝ φ x (basisVec j)`. The proof is the current testSpatialDerivative body with the `hinv` rewrite removed. Then spatialPartial_pullback ends, after `rw [hfun, hspace]`, with `exact fderiv_spatialPullback_apply μ hμ z₀.1 hslice j z.1`. The goal's RHS `μ⁻¹ * spatialPartial ψ j z` unfolds definitionally to the lemma's RHS. In spatialSecondPartial_pullback, hderiv' becomes `fderiv_spatialPullback_apply μ hμ z₀.1 hslice j z.1` directly. That removes the 14-line `fderiv_comp` block from spatialPartial_pullback and the `testSpatialInverse_eq` rewrite and `simpa` from spatialSecondPartial_pullback.
findings.benefit: The scaling-derivative argument is stated and proved once. Both pullback theorems become short reductions to it. Any change to the derivative argument is then made in one place.

findings.excerpt:
have hopen : (tsupport ψ)ᶜ ∈ 𝓝 z :=
    (isClosed_tsupport ψ).isOpen_compl.mem_nhds hz
findings.problem: The three lemmas have the same proof. Each proves `(tsupport ψ)ᶜ ∈ 𝓝 z` (hopen) and pulls it back along a slice map such as `x ↦ (x, z.2)` using `hmap.continuousAt.preimage_mem_nhds`. It then gets an eventual equality to 0 on the slice, rewrites with `hev.fderiv_eq, fderiv_const_apply`, and finishes with `simp`. The first two repeat the `by_contra`/`subset_tsupport` argument, once per slice. The second-derivative lemma repeats the whole pipeline a second time, with `hzero` in place of the support argument. The real content is simple: if f is eventually 0 near z, then each partial derivative of f at z is 0. This is written out three times, and the result is re-exposed through three `_public` wrappers.
findings.proposed_change:
Prove two lemmas on the open-neighbourhood form: `spatialPartial_eq_zero_of_eventuallyEq {f : Vec3 × ℝ → ℝ} {z} (h : f =ᶠ[𝓝 z] fun _ => 0) (i) : spatialPartial f i z = 0` and `timePartial_eq_zero_of_eventuallyEq ... : timePartial f z = 0`. Each does the slice pullback with `hmap.continuousAt.preimage_mem_nhds h`, then `hev.fderiv_eq, fderiv_const_apply, simp`. Then:
- spatialPartial: pass `h := filter_upwards [hopen] with w hw; exact not_mem_tsupport... (Function.notMem_support / `image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport` style)`. One shared `hzero : ψ =ᶠ[𝓝 z] 0` built once from `(isClosed_tsupport ψ).isOpen_compl.mem_nhds hz` would serve all three lemmas.
- timePartial: the same `hzero`.
- spatialSecondPartial: `spatialPartial_eq_zero_of_eventuallyEq (f := fun w => spatialPartial ψ i w)`, with the hypothesis from `hzero` and the first-derivative lemma at nearby points.
The unused `ContDiff` argument can go as well, together with the `_public` aliases if the private versions are made public.
findings.benefit: The neighbourhood-and-slice argument is written once, with a more general hypothesis. The three tsupport lemmas and the second-derivative case then become a few lines each. The 50-line duplicated block and the private/`_public` pairs shrink.

findings.excerpt:
have hs : Measurable (scalingSpace μ z₀.1) := by
      exact (measurable_const_add z₀.1).comp (measurable_const_smul μ)
findings.problem: Both theorems contain the same inline proof that `scalingParabolic μ z₀` is measurable. Each has an identical `hs : Measurable (scalingSpace …)` and `ht : Measurable (scalingTime …)`, followed by `(hs.comp measurable_fst).prodMk (ht.comp measurable_snd)`. The integral version adds `.aemeasurable`. ScalingInvarianceBasic.lean already has a private `scalingParabolic_continuous` that proves a continuity version of the same fact with a separate chain of `.comp`/`prodMk` terms. So three places repeat the componentwise decomposition.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma next to scalingParabolic_eq, for example `theorem scalingParabolic_measurable (μ : ℝ) (z₀ : ParabolicPoint) : Measurable (scalingParabolic μ z₀)`. Prove it by `rw [scalingParabolic_eq]` followed by the existing hs/ht/prodMk term, or via `(scalingParabolic_continuous μ z₀).measurable` if that lemma is made non-private. In integral_comp_scaling_test, use `(scalingParabolic_measurable μ z₀).aemeasurable` for hmeas. In integrable_comp_scaling_test, use `hs.comp_measurable (scalingParabolic_measurable μ z₀)`.
findings.benefit: The measurability argument is stated once, and the two integral-transformation theorems read as their measure-theoretic content only. Later uses of the scaling map get a reusable lemma.
